```python
# Exact finite forward chaining with explicit negation.
# "Lost her keys" means she does not have her keys.
# "Convince" and "persuade" denote the same relation here.

def literal(predicate, *args, negative=False):
    return (predicate, args, negative)

def opposite(item):
    predicate, args, negative = item
    return (predicate, args, not negative)

facts = {
    literal("wants_to_see", "badger", "seahorse"),
    literal("name", "bulldog", "Meadow"),
    literal("has_keys", "bulldog", negative=True),
    literal("location", "bulldog", "Argentina"),
    literal("money", "crow", 66),
    literal("trades_piece", "gadwall", "reindeer"),
    literal("money", "mermaid", 74),
    literal("name", "seahorse", "Milo"),
    literal("hides_cards_from", "dragon", "flamingo", negative=True),
    literal("persuades", "vampire", "seal", negative=True),
}

# Compute the arithmetic and string antecedents exactly.
money = {"crow": 66, "mermaid": 74}
names = {"bulldog": "Meadow", "seahorse": "Milo"}
if money["mermaid"] > money["crow"]:
    facts.add(literal("has_more_money_than", "mermaid", "crow"))
if names["bulldog"][0] == names["seahorse"][0]:
    facts.add(literal("same_name_initial", "bulldog", "seahorse"))

rules = []

def add_rule(name, antecedents, conclusion):
    rules.append((name, frozenset(antecedents), conclusion))

add_rule("Rule1", [literal("location", "bulldog", "Africa")],
         literal("pays", "bulldog", "badger", negative=True))
add_rule("Rule2", [
    literal("hides_cards_from", "vampire", "fish"),
    literal("creates_castle_for", "mermaid", "fish"),
], literal("hides_cards_from", "fish", "otter", negative=True))

# Ground Rule3 over every animal appearing in the question.
animals = {
    "badger", "bulldog", "crow", "gadwall", "reindeer", "mermaid",
    "seahorse", "dragon", "flamingo", "vampire", "seal", "fish", "otter",
}
for animal in sorted(animals):
    add_rule("Rule3:" + animal,
             [literal("persuades", animal, "seal", negative=True)],
             literal("hides_cards_from", animal, "fish"))

add_rule("Rule4", [literal("has_more_money_than", "mermaid", "crow")],
         literal("creates_castle_for", "mermaid", "fish"))
add_rule("Rule5", [literal("has_keys", "bulldog", negative=True)],
         literal("pays", "bulldog", "badger"))
add_rule("Rule6", [literal("same_name_initial", "bulldog", "seahorse")],
         literal("pays", "bulldog", "badger", negative=True))

preferred = {("Rule1", "Rule5"), ("Rule6", "Rule5")}
known = set(facts)
while True:
    applicable = [r for r in rules if r[1] <= known]
    conclusions = set()
    for name, antecedents, head in applicable:
        defeated = any(
            (other_name, name) in preferred and other_head == opposite(head)
            for other_name, _, other_head in applicable
        )
        if not defeated:
            conclusions.add(head)
    expanded = known | conclusions
    if expanded == known:
        break
    known = expanded

query = literal("hides_cards_from", "fish", "otter")
positive = query in known
negative = opposite(query) in known

print("Mermaid money > crow money:", money["mermaid"] > money["crow"])
print("Vampire hides cards from fish:",
      literal("hides_cards_from", "vampire", "fish") in known)
print("Mermaid creates castle for fish:",
      literal("creates_castle_for", "mermaid", "fish") in known)
print("Fish hides cards from otter:", positive)
print("Fish does not hide cards from otter:", negative)

if positive and negative:
    print("UNSUPPORTED: both polarities derived")
    print("CHECK UNKNOWN")
else:
    expected = "proved" if positive else "disproved" if negative else "unknown"
    submitted = "proved"
    print("Expected result:", expected)
    print("Submitted result:", submitted)
    print("CHECK PASS" if expected == submitted else "CHECK FAIL")
```
